claims.text: The additively manufactured Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 alloy has an FCC matrix in its starting state.
Lattice distortion governs degradation of the additively manufactured Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 alloy during elevated-temperature gas exposure.
Lattice distortion suppresses diffusion by increasing vacancy-formation energies and elemental migration barriers.
Diffusion suppression retards sustained oxide-scale growth during elevated-temperature oxidation.
The proposed degradation mechanism applies to exposure in either oxidizing or reducing gases.
The relevant exposure regime is above 1100 °C.
The proposed behavior has an applicable boundary below 1100 °C.
Relative to conventional MCrAlY, the target alloy will exhibit reduced degradation at temperatures above 1100 °C.
Relative to conventional MCrAlY, the target alloy will exhibit less catastrophic oxide-scale failure or spallation.
Conventional MCrAlY has an approximate 1100 °C temperature ceiling because oxidation and spallation accelerate above it.
Catastrophic failure may occur when accumulated elastic strain energy at the oxide/alloy interface exceeds the fracture toughness of the oxide or interface.
Diffusion suppression itself leads to catastrophic failure.
The exact temperature threshold for catastrophic failure is uncertain.
The hypothesis is falsified if the target alloy does not have a significantly lower oxidation-rate constant than MCrAlY or does not show significantly improved spallation behavior above 1100 °C.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis says diffusion suppression leads to catastrophic failure, whereas the predicted outcome says it reduces catastrophic failure.
The stated test condition is above 1100 °C, while the stated applicability boundary is below 1100 °C; the hypothesis does not explain how these nonoverlapping regimes relate.
